activation.details: Restart the Omarchy shell (omarchy-restart-shell) so Powerbar reloads the widget and re-measures its slot.

payload.effects: Powerbar no longer applies the 160 px free-text cap to the widget on a horizontal bar, so the slot grows to the widget's full readout. According to the same source, vertical bars do not apply the cap at all.
payload.explanation: Give the widget two or more click targets so Powerbar treats it as a compound slot, like the workspaces widget, which keeps its full measured length. Each qs.Ui WidgetButton registers itself as a click target with the bar it is given, so splitting the readout into several WidgetButtons that all call the same handler is enough. Powerbar itself is not changed.

steps: Split the widget's readout into two or more qs.Ui WidgetButton items (labelVisible: false, fixedWidth from each button's own content) and pass each one the bar it was given (bar: root.bar) so it registers as a click target.
Lay the buttons out in a Row or Grid and set the widget root's implicitWidth and implicitHeight from that container.
Send every button's onPressed to the same handler so the widget still acts as one control, and anchor any popup to the container rather than to one button.
Restart the shell with omarchy-restart-shell so Powerbar loads the new widget code and measures the slot again.
Take a screenshot of the bar (for example with grim) and confirm the whole readout is visible.

payload.rollback: Go back to a single WidgetButton and restart the shell; the 160 px cap applies again.
payload.validation_plan: After the shell restart, screenshot the bar and confirm the full readout is visible; then click each part of the widget and confirm it still opens the widget's popup.
